justification: Coordinate-first parcel resolution. When the brief has a trusted pin (Google Places lat/lng) but no prop_id, resolve the parcel by point-in-cadastre (NSW Property layer) + the SAME parcel-identity cross-check, before the fuzzy text geocode. Fixes valid addresses that the text search + GATE-0 false-closed, without weakening wrong-parcel protection. Live-verified end-to-end: 2/45 Alt St (was a text false-close) now resolves; 22 Northwood (bad pin) still 422.

pre_impl.existing_data: The brief page POSTs address+lat+lng but no prop_id; _resolve_address only used lat/lng when prop_id was ALSO present, so it discarded the Google pin and re-geocoded the string via the fuzzy Portal /address search. NSW_Land_Parcel_Property_Theme/FeatureServer/12 point-in-polygon returns the propId that matches the Portal (verified 14 Stanley=1456609) plus the parcel's cadastre address.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: 'covered by Google autocomplete' did not mean 'resolved reliably' — the backend threw the coordinate away. The fix uses the coordinate that was already provided.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: prior-art-checked (ack in code): no existing coordinate->propId resolver — frontend TS fetchers and the Python overlay/strata point queries don't return a propId. New resolve_propid_by_point sits beside resolve_address and shares _portal_get + the extracted _lot_centroid_wkt + parcel_identity_match.
pre_impl.external_source_error: resolve_propid_by_point wraps the HTTP call in try/except -> None on any error/0-features/ambiguity; _resolve_address then falls back to the existing text resolver, which keeps its own GATE-0, ending in an honest 422. No new failure mode is introduced.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A (backend Python). No frontend change; the page already sends lat/lng.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: valid addresses (incl. strata units) blanked because the text geocoder returned a neighbouring parcel and GATE-0 fail-closed. After: the pin resolves the correct parcel by point + identity cross-check; a pin on the wrong parcel still yields no match -> text fallback -> 422 (never wrong-parcel data).

functions.name: resolve_propid_by_point
functions.input: lat, lng (WGS84 pin) and the requested address string
functions.output: (prop_id, lat, lng, lot_wkt) iff exactly one distinct propId's cadastre address passes parcel_identity_match; else None
functions.if_none: returns None on no-feature / address-mismatch / ambiguous distinct propIds / HTTP error, so the caller falls back to the text resolver

functions.name: _resolve_address
functions.output: (prop_id, lat, lng, lot_wkt); coordinate-first when a pin is present, text fallback otherwise
functions.if_none: if neither path resolves a valid NSW coordinate it raises HTTP 422 (unchanged honest fail-closed)

values: N/A - no regulatory values. propId and geometry come from the NSW cadastre/portal; nothing is hardcoded.
queries: N/A - no database query. Adds one ArcGIS point-in-polygon HTTP call to the NSW cadastre Property layer (reuses the existing /lot fetch for geometry).

break_it.scenario: The Google pin lands on a neighbouring parcel
break_it.what_happens: naively trusting the point would serve the WRONG parcel as authoritative (the exact thing GATE-0 #514 prevents)
break_it.repro: test_wrong_parcel_is_rejected + live 22 Northwood: the cadastre address fails parcel_identity_match so no propId survives
break_it.how: resolve only when a matched propId exists; otherwise None -> text fallback -> 422. Verified live: 22 Northwood still 422

break_it.scenario: A strata/apartment block returns many address points at the pin
break_it.what_happens: multiple features could be read as ambiguous and drop a valid address
break_it.how: matched features collapse to a set of distinct propIds; one distinct id -> resolve. Live: 5/1 Treacy, 2/45 Alt resolve

break_it.scenario: Two parcels genuinely share the same address tokens but different propIds
break_it.what_happens: picking either would be a guess
break_it.how: len(distinct matched propIds) != 1 returns None -> text fallback (no guess)

break_it.scenario: The cadastre Property endpoint is down, slow, or returns malformed JSON
break_it.what_happens: an unguarded call would raise and break resolution
break_it.how: the call is wrapped (timeout 15s) -> None -> existing text resolver runs as before

break_it.scenario: A unit address ('2/45 Alt St') whose cadastre parcel is the base property ('45 Alt St')
break_it.what_happens: a strict match would reject a valid strata unit (re-creating the false-close)
break_it.how: normalize_addr_tokens strips the unit prefix on both sides, so the unit matches its base-property address

post_merge.other_repo: N/A - backend runs on Railway (nswcompliance), auto-deploys from GitHub on merge.
post_merge.manual_verify: In the brief, pick a strata-unit or text-fuzzy address from Google autocomplete (e.g. 2/45 Alt Street, Ashfield) that previously blanked — it should now resolve. A pin that lands off-parcel still yields the honest 'could not determine coordinates' 422.
